_what: PROPOSED registration of rapp-metrics/1.0 into kody-w/rapp-spine/registry.json. This file is a patch description, not a spine artifact — nothing here has been applied. `registry_entry` is the exact object to append to registry.json's top-level `registry` array; `router_entries` are the exact objects to append to its top-level `router` array. Both were shaped against the live registry.json (spec rapp-spine/1.0, generated 2026-07-11) read in a scratch clone on 2026-08-02.
_shape_note: registry.json's `registry` array carries two entry shapes and both are legal: 35 entries use the 6-key protocol shape {spec_id, repo, layer, purpose, when_to_use, entry_point} and 24 use the 6-key spec-mirror shape {spec_id, repo, layer, role, raw_url, entry_point}. rapp-metrics is a protocol with its own repo, not a spec text hosted inside rapp-spine, so it takes the FIRST shape — key order below matches the order those entries are serialized in (spec_id, repo, layer, purpose, when_to_use, entry_point). Router entries use {situation, use[], why}; `use` is always an array of strings even when it holds one element.
_layer_choice: distribution. rapp-metrics/1.0 profiles rapp-static-api/1.0 ('the repo IS the API'), which the distribution layer summary already names as 'the zero-server convention every catalog builds on', and RAR — the reference implementation — is registered at layer distribution as rapp-registry/1.0. The considered alternative was the map layer ('orientation + observability'), and it is wrong: that layer observes SPEC AND VERSION drift across the estate (rapp-god, rapp-map), not usage of a surface by people. Matches the layer the spec itself declares in SPEC.md §15.

registry_entry.purpose: Real utilization/impact numbers for surfaces with no backend. GitHub Discussions supply per-subject identity, spam control and per-user-deduped reaction counters; a scheduled workflow folds them into one byte-stable JSON snapshot any static page reads with a plain GET. No server, no auth, no PII, no timestamps (the git history of the file IS the time series). Founding tenet: THE ACTOR DETERMINES THE LANE — an automated actor may never touch a human counter, and a human acting at the bot layer always counts. Machine reviewers are a first-class output in a structurally separate editorial lane (rapp-metrics-editorial/1.0) that can never enter the human counters; agent-authored CONTENT still earns real human numbers.
registry_entry.when_to_use: When a static RAPP surface (registry, tool gallery, video channel, egg hub, store) needs defensible usage numbers and you refuse to run a server or hold user data. Also the governing spec whenever an automation is about to write to a counter — the bot-reaction prohibition is normative (SPEC.md §10.3, E11-E13). Reference impls: RAR (subject = agent, running), rapp-vision (subject = video, in flight).
registry_entry.entry_point: Implement one function — enumerate() -> [{subject_id, title, url, digest}] — declare a profile, run the collector on a cron. SPEC.md in repo; §1 is the founding tenet (the law), §5 the provider interface, §9 the invariants, §10 the editorial lane, §13 the 52-item conformance checklist.

router_entries.situation: How do I measure usage of my RAPP surface — real numbers I can defend in a meeting — when it is static, hydra-served, and has no server, no database and no accounts?
router_entries.why: GitHub is the backend you already have: Discussions give one permanent public thread per subject, and reactions are deduped per user BY THE PLATFORM — so every count means PEOPLE, NOT CLICKS by construction, with nothing to defend. A cron folds them into one byte-stable snapshot committed only when a number actually moved, so the git log becomes the time series. The law that makes any of it trustworthy: THE ACTOR DETERMINES THE LANE, NEVER THE SUBJECT — no bot, service account, app installation or CI token may ever add a reaction (one bot upvote makes every number a lie), while a human acting at the bot layer counts fully (200 people upvoting an agent-generated video is 200 people). Machine reviews are first-class but live in a walled editorial lane, attributed to a reviewer id and rubric version and rendered as machine-authored — and human reactions to a machine review count as human signal ABOUT THE REVIEWER, which is how a wrong rubric becomes visible.

router_entries.situation: I want to publish video (or any media) on a platform I OWN, served as static files from my own repo — a channel, not an upload to someone else's site — and then know whether anyone actually watched it.
use: rapp-hydra/1.0 (if the channel must survive a takedown)
router_entries.why: GAP-FIX ROUTE. Publishing media you own is a STATIC-FILE concern, not a compute concern: you push a channel.json to a public repo and the single-file player streams it — no server, no account, no build step, and every src/thumb resolves relative to that file's URL so the channel plays from any host. Before this entry the router had no situation mentioning video, channel or media at all (verified: 0 occurrences of 'video', 'vision', 'media' or 'channel.json' anywhere in registry.json), so a crawler asking for 'a platform I own that hosts my videos' fell through to the nearest lexical match — the Tier-2 entry promising 'an always-on cloud body' — and was sent to CommunityRAPP on Azure Functions. That is a wrong answer twice over: it provisions cloud compute for a problem that is a GET of a JSON file, and it abandons the local-first property that made the surface worth owning. Measurement rides the same static substrate via rapp-metrics/1.0 — and note the id trap: a video id is unique only inside its own channel.json, so the metrics subject_id MUST be channel-qualified as <channel.id>/<video.id>.

_companion_registry_entry_optional._why_optional: NOT part of the required rapp-metrics registration, and it is a separate judgment call for Kody. But without it the second router entry above routes to a repo the spine does not index at all — rapp-vision appears nowhere in registry.json. A router `use` that names an unregistered protocol is a dangling route, which is the failure mode the spine exists to prevent. Land it with the router entry, or drop the rapp-vision names from that entry's `use` and point only at rapp-static-api/1.0 + rapp-metrics/1.0.
_companion_registry_entry_optional._status_caveat: Grounded in a scratch clone read on 2026-08-02 while a parallel session was actively writing that repo. The channel/network schema strings and the single-file-player claim are read from committed files (channel.json, channels.json, README.md, index.html). Do not treat the metrics half as shipped: rapp-vision's own README still says it has no metrics implementation, while scripts/rapp_metrics.py, .github/workflows/metrics.yml and state/metrics.json now exist in the working tree. Confirm live before publishing.
_companion_registry_entry_optional.purpose: A local-first video platform: one HTML file, no server, no database, no account, no build step. A channel is a channel.json published to any public repo (rapp-vision-channel/1.0); the network is just a list of channel URLs (rapp-vision-network/1.0), and anyone can run their own registry or add a channel locally without permission. Entries may be ordinary video files OR 'live replay' — a few KB of recorded interactions the player replays against the REAL application in an iframe, so a viewer can pause, take the wheel and fork the script. Viewer history, watch-later and likes stay in localStorage and export as JSON.
_companion_registry_entry_optional.when_to_use: When you want to publish media on a surface you own and can hand to anyone, instead of uploading to a platform that owns the audience — or when a product demo needs to be interruptible rather than watched. Pair with rapp-metrics/1.0 for defensible view/endorsement numbers.
_companion_registry_entry_optional.entry_point: Copy template/channel.json into any public repo, set schema/id/name and the entries, then play it at https://kody-w.github.io/rapp-vision/ — or clone rapp-vision next to the repos its live channels drive and serve the PARENT directory (python3 -m http.server 8000). Open a PR against channels.json to be listed on the default network.

steps: 1. Append `registry_entry` to the top-level `registry` array. Existing entries are grouped loosely by layer rather than sorted, so append near the other `distribution` entries (RAR / rapp-burrow sit at the tail).
2. Append both objects in `router_entries` to the top-level `router` array (currently 32 entries).

3. Add the string "rapp-metrics/1.0" to the `protocols` array of the layer object whose `layer` field is "distribution (package, name, ship, install)". Note that array is already non-exhaustive — rapp-registry/1.0 is registered at layer distribution but absent from it — so this is tidiness, not a correctness requirement.
4. If landing the companion entry, append it too and add "rapp-vision-channel/1.0 (kody-w/rapp-vision)" to the same `protocols` array.
5. Bump the top-level `generated` field (currently "2026-07-11") to the date of the change.

6. Re-run whatever rebuilds llms.txt / llms-full.txt / coverage.json / SPINE.md from registry.json in that repo (render_spine.py, verify_spine.py) so the derived surfaces do not go stale — rapp-canon/1.0 §4 requires the change-set to leave no spec stale.
_apply.not_done_here: No commit, no push, no PR, no edit to any file in kody-w/rapp-spine. This file is the patch description only.

_reconcile: MUST-FIX BEFORE APPLYING — the spec's own copy of this block is not registry-shaped. rapp-metrics/SPEC.md carries a proposed registry block (§15 when first read, renumbered to §16 during this session). As of 2026-08-02 21:49 that block carries a SEVENTH key, `founding_tenet`, which appears in NO entry of the live registry.json — every one of the 59 entries uses either the 6-key protocol shape or the 6-key spec-mirror shape. Appending a 7-key object would make rapp-metrics the only non-conforming entry in the file and would break any consumer that assumes the two known shapes. `registry_entry` above therefore folds the tenet into `purpose` instead, keeping the shape exact. Reconcile in one direction before shipping: either update SPEC.md's block to match this object, or drop `founding_tenet` from it — but do not ship both as-is, or the spec and the spine disagree on day one, which is exactly the drift the estate runs four detection legs to catch.

Section numbers moved under me during this session (SPEC.md was restructured so the tenet became §1). `entry_point` above cites the NEW numbering — §4 provider is now §5, §8 invariants is now §9, §9 editorial is now §10, §12 checklist is now §13. Re-verify the section numbers in `entry_point` against SPEC.md at the moment of publish; a router entry that cites a wrong section is worse than one that cites none.

Neither the registry entry nor the router entries can be verified live: kody-w/rapp-metrics did not exist as a repo at the time of writing, so `repo` and `entry_point` describe the intended publish target, not a fetched URL. Verify both resolve before or immediately after the repo is created.
